sections.h2: What does the Brunswick County Register of Deeds handle?
sections.html:
This office keeps the land records for Brunswick County. Deeds, deeds of trust, easements, maps, releases and satisfactions all pass through it, and so do marriage licenses, certified copies and oaths. Voters choose the register for a four-year term. The staff can file what you bring but cannot advise you or draft the paper.

Brunswick was carved out in 1764 from parts of Bladen and New Hanover, and the vault still holds grants, indentures and conveyances from that first period. Modern filings include restrictions and covenants, assumed names, UCC statements and powers of attorney next to the steady stream of deeds from coastal home sales.

A seller here ends up at this counter, either in person, by mail or through a title firm. Until the buyer's deed is on the record, the sale is not protected against outside claims, so the practical details below deserve a read before closing day.

sections.h2: Where is the Brunswick County Register of Deeds and what are its hours?
sections.html:
Look for Building I at 75 Courthouse Drive NE, Bolivia, NC 28422. Call 910-253-2690, or the toll-free alternate 877-625-9310; postal mail is addressed to PO Box 87 in Bolivia. Each service keeps its own window.

  • Recording desk: opens 8:30 am, closes 4:30 pm, weekdays.
  • Land and vital records: opens 8:30 am, closes 5 pm, weekdays.
  • Marriage licenses: by appointment, 8:30 am until 4:30 pm.
  • Passports: by appointment, 8:30 am until 3:30 pm.

You can hand a document over at the counter, post it to the box, or ship it by courier to the Courthouse Drive street address. The county holiday calendar applies to the recording desk.

sections.h2: What does Brunswick County require before it will record a deed?
sections.html:
A short county checklist governs what the clerks accept. Only an original, or a certified copy that carries the original signature, can go on the record.

  • The recording fee, paid by check to BCROD, plus a stamped return envelope.
  • The preparer's name and address on page one.
  • Names and addresses of both seller and buyer on the face of the deed.
  • Signatures and a notary seal that reads clearly.
  • The delinquent tax certification step the county lists for all deeds.
  • Excise tax, which the county explains as $2 per $1,000 of the sales price.

Layout counts too. Under G.S. 161-14(b), as the county quotes it, use letter or legal paper, leave a three-inch blank band on page one, keep half-inch margins elsewhere, print in black on white at 9 points or more, and use one side of each sheet. A deed outside those limits is still accepted, with a $25 charge added.

sections.h2: How much will filing a deed in Brunswick County run?
sections.html:
Two sources set the price: a statewide schedule and the county's copy rates. The lines below follow the wording of the official pages.

Charges tied to a Brunswick County deed, with where each is printed
ItemChargeWhere printed
General instrument$26.00 covers pages 1 to 15; $4.00 for every page past thatG.S. 161-10
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 covers pages 1 to 35; $4.00 for every page past thatG.S. 161-10
Satisfaction of a mortgageNo chargeCounty recording page
Document outside the format standards$25.00 extraCounty recording page
Certified copy$5.00 for page one, $2.00 per later pageCounty records page
Plain copy25 cents a page, with $1.00 or a stamped envelope added by mailCounty records page
Excise tax$1.00 per $500County records page

Plats are separate. A freestanding plat must be 18 by 24 inches on film or mylar and cleared by the county review officer, and the state schedule lists plats at $21.00 per sheet.

sections.h2: Who pays the Brunswick County excise tax?
sections.html:
The seller owes it. G.S. 105-228.30 makes the transferor pay the register before recording, at one dollar per $500 of value, counting any leftover fraction.

The county's records page lists earlier rates, including $0.50 and $0.55 per $500 for stretches between 1932 and 1991, which explains the different stamps on old deeds. Half of each collection stays in county government and half is sent on to the state.

A separate hurdle is unpaid property tax. The county names tax certification as a recording condition, and an electronically filed deed must state that any delinquent taxes will be paid to the county tax collector by the closing attorney when funds are disbursed. If back taxes are owed, request a payoff figure from the collector early, and have your attorney show the excise line on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: Can a lender or title firm e-record in Brunswick County?
sections.html:
Yes. Businesses and lending institutions can e-record through Internet Technologies, Inc. (Inttek) during the usual weekday recording hours. Private owners normally file on paper.

  • Card and PayPal payments add 6% of the document's total cost plus $0.50.
  • ACH funds moved into escrow add 2.5% of the amount escrowed.
  • Regular recording fees remain due on top of the vendor charge.
  • Maps can be e-recorded when they show an existing parcel.

An e-recorded deed must open with a prepared-by statement naming a North Carolina attorney and the delinquent tax wording, and every e-filing needs the submitter statement tied to the county's submitter agreement. Ask your closing firm which route it uses, because electronic filing is how many deeds reach the office the day they are signed.

sections.h2: How can I search Brunswick County deeds and get copies?
sections.html:
The county's online search covers filings from September 1939 forward. Fill in any one field, such as the buyer's name, a date range, a document type or a book and page, and each hit offers a PDF download.

Index books from 1932 to 1953 are scanned as legacy indexes, so you find the name alphabetically and then type the book and page into the search page. For a certified copy, mail a written request and payment to BCROD at the PO Box, or order through the search site.

Two protections are worth knowing. Anyone may ask the office to strip a Social Security number or bank or card number from an image shown online, using the redaction form. And the register offers a free fraud alert that sends a notice whenever a document is recorded under your name, which suits owners of vacant or inherited houses.

sections.h2: How is Brunswick County changing, according to the Census?
sections.html:
Growth is the story here. The Census Bureau estimated 174,702 people in July 2025, compared with 107,431 at the 2010 count and a 27.8% gain over the 2020 base. People 65 and older are 36.6% of the total. Housing units number 116,023 on 850.08 square miles of land.

The 2020 to 2024 survey puts the owner share at 84.6%, the middle home value at $349,800 and the middle household income at $77,024. Typical gross rent is $1,351. With 4,457 building permits in 2025, new construction keeps adding deeds to the office's workload.

Source: Census QuickFacts for Brunswick County.

sections.h2: Why does recording matter when I sell a Brunswick County house?
sections.html:
Recording sets the pecking order of claims. Under G.S. 47-18, an unregistered conveyance carries no weight against lien creditors or paying buyers, and priority runs by registration time.

For that reason a buyer's attorney keeps the funds back until the deed and new loan papers are filed. On your side, an old mortgage should show a recorded satisfaction. The lender files it, the county charges nothing, and a quick search of your own deed confirms it is there.

Inherited houses, liens and unpaid taxes slow the process, so raise them with the closing attorney early. A cash buyer's offer still needs the same deed, the same tax certification and the same excise payment.

faqs.q: Where does a Brunswick County deed get filed?
faqs.a: At Building I, 75 Courthouse Drive NE, Bolivia, NC 28422, or by mail to PO Box 87. Recording hours are 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, and the phone is 910-253-2690.

faqs.q: How is the Brunswick County deed stamp tax figured?
faqs.a: The rate is $1.00 per $500 of value conveyed, a figure the county also words as $2 per $1,000, and the seller pays it up front.

faqs.q: What is the fee to file a mortgage in Brunswick County?
faqs.a: State law sets $64.00 through page 35 and $4.00 for each page beyond. Filing the satisfaction after payoff is free.

faqs.q: Can a homeowner e-record a Brunswick County deed?
faqs.a: Only businesses and lenders can, through Inttek. Vendor fees run 6% plus $0.50 for cards or 2.5% for ACH escrow, in addition to normal recording fees.

faqs.q: How do I order a certified deed copy from Bolivia?
faqs.a: Mail a written request with payment to BCROD at the PO Box, or click the request link in the online search results. Page one is $5.00 and later pages are $2.00 each.
